title: The Best Sony Lenses For Concert Photography
summary: The best Sony lenses for concerts in 2026: bright aperture, fast autofocus and options for every venue and shooting position.
body_markdown:
Concert photography moves fast. You may be photographing a performer in a dark club one minute, then working under rapidly changing spotlights, haze and LED walls the next. The best concert lenses combine bright apertures for difficult light, fast and reliable autofocus for performers in motion, and focal lengths that help you tell the whole story – from a crowd-wide establishing frame to a tight, expressive portrait from the photo pit.


For Sony Alpha photographers, the E-mount lineup offers compelling options for every venue and shooting position. Below are some of the best Sony lenses for concert photography, with the features that make each one shine under stage lights. Explore and compare the complete lineup at[alphauniverse.com/lenses](https://alphauniverse.com/lenses/) .


#### What are the best lenses for concert photography?


##### 1.[Sony 16-35mm f/2.8 G Master II](https://electronics.sony.com/imaging/lenses/all-e-mount/p/sel1635gm2?utm_source=AlphaUniverse&utm_medium=Web&utm_campaign=Article)


###### Why It’s Great For Concert Photography


When you are close to the stage, the[16-35mm f/2.8 GM II](https://electronics.sony.com/imaging/lenses/all-e-mount/p/sel1635gm2?utm_source=AlphaUniverse&utm_medium=Web&utm_campaign=Article) is a powerful storytelling lens. At the wide end, it can take in the scale of the venue, the crowd and the lighting design; at 35mm, it creates a more intimate perspective of a performer without stepping back. The constant f/2.8 aperture provides the light-gathering ability needed in challenging concert environments.


###### Standout Features


- 16-35mm range covers dramatic wide stage scenes, crowd interaction and close photo-pit perspectives
- Constant f/2.8 aperture supports faster shutter speeds in dim venues
- Fast, quiet autofocus helps maintain focus as artists move through changing light
- Compact, lighter second-generation design reduces fatigue during long sets
- Refined optics and coatings help preserve contrast when working with spotlights and backlighting


###### Creator Reviews


"Great for both landscapes and lifestyle shots. It’s a lightweight lens with corner-to-corner sharpness and no chromatic aberration. It’s the perfect lens to really open up an environment." –[Mickey Pierre-Louis](https://alphauniverse.com/member/#/itchyeyephotos) ,[What’s In My Bag: The Ultimate Camera Kit For Music & Portrait Shoots](https://alphauniverse.com/stories/whats-in-my-bag-the-ultimate-camera-kit-for-music-and-portrait-shoots/)


Kendrick Lamar - photo by Mickey Pierre-Louis. Sony Alpha 7R IV. Sony 16-35mm f/2.8 G Master II.


"Really great for crowd shots and getting the scale of a performance." –[Greg Noire](https://www.instagram.com/gregnoire/) ,[Go Inside Greg Noire’s Ultimate Concert Photography Kit](https://alphauniverse.com/stories/go-inside-greg-noires-ultimate-concert-photography-kit/)


Photo by Greg Noire. Alpha 7 III. 16-35mm f/2.8 G Master. 1/160-sec., f/2.8, ISO 2500


##### [2. Sony 28-70mm f/2 G Master](https://electronics.sony.com/imaging/lenses/all-e-mount/p/sel2870gm?utm_source=AlphaUniverse&utm_medium=Web&utm_campaign=Article)


###### Why It’s Great For Concert Photography


The[28-70mm f/2 GM](https://electronics.sony.com/imaging/lenses/all-e-mount/p/sel2870gm?utm_source=AlphaUniverse&utm_medium=Web&utm_campaign=Article) is an especially versatile choice for photographers who want the flexibility of a standard zoom with an extra stop of light over traditional f/2.8 options. That f/2 aperture is valuable in low-light clubs and theaters, where it can help you protect shutter speed and ISO while creating more subject separation. Its range is ideal for full-body performance images, portraits and in-the-moment details from the photo pit.


###### Standout Features


- Constant f/2 maximum aperture gives valuable low-light headroom throughout the zoom range
- 28-70mm coverage works for stage-wide frames, mid-length portraits and details
- Four XD linear motors deliver fast, responsive autofocus for moving performers
- Nano AR Coating II helps reduce flare and ghosting from direct stage lighting
- Internal focusing keeps handling stable while shooting


###### Creator Reviews


"It’s like having a prime lens at each focal length. So it’s really cool for shooting an artist directly, or getting really cool, isolated moments from the crowd." –[Greg Noire](https://www.instagram.com/gregnoire/) ,[Go Inside Greg Noire’s Ultimate Concert Photography Kit](https://alphauniverse.com/stories/go-inside-greg-noires-ultimate-concert-photography-kit/)


Photo by Greg Noire. Alpha 1 II. 28-70mm f/2 G Master. 1/1250-sec., f/2, ISO 100


##### [3. Sony 24-70mm f/2.8 G Master II](https://electronics.sony.com/imaging/lenses/all-e-mount/p/sel2470gm2?utm_source=AlphaUniverse&utm_medium=Web&utm_campaign=Article)


###### Why It’s Great For Concert Photography


For photographers who need one dependable lens that can handle most of a show, the[24-70mm f/2.8 GM II](https://electronics.sony.com/imaging/lenses/all-e-mount/p/sel2470gm2?utm_source=AlphaUniverse&utm_medium=Web&utm_campaign=Article) is the workhorse. Its useful wide-to-short-telephoto range makes it easy to move between environmental frames, full-length shots and tighter compositions without changing lenses during a critical moment. It is also notably compact and light for its class—an advantage when you are working a long night on your feet.


###### Standout Features


- 24-70mm range handles the core focal lengths used for live-music coverage
- Constant f/2.8 aperture maintains exposure consistency as you zoom
- Four XD linear motors support quick, accurate autofocus
- Approximate 695g weight makes it the smallest and lightest f/2.8 24-70mm zoom in its class
- Excellent choice for hybrid creators working in both stills and video


###### Creator Reviews


"If I could only shoot with one lens I would choose the 24-70mm. It is the perfect mid-range zoom lens to own as you can get wide shots at 24mm and close shots at 70mm. The 2.8 aperture is perfect for low light situations." –[Drew Hallé](https://www.instagram.com/drewwhalle/) ,[What’s In My Bag: Two Cameras & Three Zooms For Dynamic Music Photography](https://alphauniverse.com/stories/whats-in-my-bag-2-cameras-and-3-zooms-for-dynamic-music-photography/)


Photo by Drew Hallé. Sony Alpha 7 III. Sony 24-70mm f/2.8 G Master. 1/320-sec., f/2.8, ISO 800


"I always have the 24-70mm with me at all times. It’s just the most versatile zoom range for any situation. It can get both wide-angle shots and also portrait zoom lengths on it." –[Serena Yang](https://alphauniverse.com/member/#/serena-yang/) ,[Best Lenses For Concert Photography: Serena Yang’s Top Picks](https://alphauniverse.com/stories/best-lenses-for-concert-photography-serena-yangs-top-picks/)


##### 4.[Sony 35mm f/1.4 G Master](https://electronics.sony.com/imaging/lenses/all-e-mount/p/sel35f14gm?utm_source=AlphaUniverse&utm_medium=Web&utm_campaign=Article)


###### Why It’s Great For Concert Photography


A fast 35mm prime is a concert-photography essential for many shooters. The[35mm f/1.4 GM](https://electronics.sony.com/imaging/lenses/all-e-mount/p/sel35f14gm?utm_source=AlphaUniverse&utm_medium=Web&utm_campaign=Article) gives a natural, immersive field of view that feels close to the energy of the performance while its bright aperture helps in the lowest light. It is a strong choice for artists at the edge of the stage, backstage storytelling and environmental portraits that preserve the mood of the room.


###### Standout Features


- Bright f/1.4 aperture helps maintain shutter speed in dark venues
- 35mm perspective creates intimate, documentary-style performance images
- 11-blade aperture produces smooth, expressive out-of-focus backgrounds
- Compact form factor is easy to carry as a second body or primary low-light lens
- G Master optics deliver sharp detail across the frame, even when used wide open


###### Creator Reviews


"If I could only shoot with one lens for the rest of my life, it would be this lens. Compact and lightweight. It mimics the field of view of the human eye without distortion." –[Mickey Pierre-Louis](https://alphauniverse.com/member/#/itchyeyephotos) ,[What’s In My Bag: The Ultimate Camera Kit For Music & Portrait Shoots](https://alphauniverse.com/stories/whats-in-my-bag-the-ultimate-camera-kit-for-music-and-portrait-shoots/)


Photo by Mickey Pierre-Louis. Sony Alpha 7R V. Sony 35mm f/1.4 G Master. 1/400-sec., f/2.8, ISO 800


##### 5.[Sony 50mm f/1.2 G Master](https://electronics.sony.com/imaging/lenses/all-e-mount/p/sel50f12gm?utm_source=AlphaUniverse&utm_medium=Web&utm_campaign=Article)


###### Why It’s Great For Concert Photography


The[50mm f/1.2 GM](https://electronics.sony.com/imaging/lenses/all-e-mount/p/sel50f12gm?utm_source=AlphaUniverse&utm_medium=Web&utm_campaign=Article) is made for those moments when the light drops and the visual focus needs to be entirely on the artist. Its ultra-bright maximum aperture lets photographers work at lower ISOs or faster shutter speeds, while creating the shallow depth of field that makes a singer, guitarist or drummer stand out from a busy stage. It is especially effective for close-range performance portraits and emotional detail shots.


###### Standout Features


- Ultra-bright f/1.2 aperture for difficult low-light scenes
- Strong subject isolation separates performers from distracting backgrounds
- Fast, precise autofocus supports reliable focus at very shallow depth of field
- G Master rendering delivers sharp subjects with smooth, rounded bokeh
- Useful 50mm perspective for portraits, half-body compositions and stage details


###### Creator Reviews


"If I had to take one lens on any shoot, it would be this one." –[Travis Ellison](https://www.instagram.com/travietrav_dmv/) ,[What's In My Bag: Travis Ellison's Kit For Capturing Sports, Entertainment & More](http://alphauniverse.com/stories/whats-in-my-bag-travis-ellisons-kit-for-capturing-sports-entertainment-and-more/)


Photo by Travis Ellison. Alpha 1. 50mm f/1.2 G Master. 1/400-sec., f/1.2, ISO 500


##### [6. Sony 85mm f/1.4 G Master II](https://electronics.sony.com/imaging/lenses/all-e-mount/p/sel85f14gm2?utm_source=AlphaUniverse&utm_medium=Web&utm_campaign=Article)


###### Why It’s Great For Concert Photography


When access is limited or the photographer is farther from the stage, the[85mm f/1.4 GM II](https://electronics.sony.com/imaging/lenses/all-e-mount/p/sel85f14gm2?utm_source=AlphaUniverse&utm_medium=Web&utm_campaign=Article) brings performers closer without sacrificing the speed needed for live music. It is a natural choice for isolating a vocalist against stage lights, capturing a musician’s expression or creating compressed portraits with beautiful background blur.


###### Standout Features


- f/1.4 aperture delivers strong low-light performance and dramatic subject separation
- 85mm focal length is ideal for tight portraits from the barricade or side stage
- Advanced autofocus improves responsiveness for performers in motion
- Lightweight, refined design makes it easier to use handheld throughout a set
- Physical aperture ring gives quick tactile exposure control


###### Creator Reviews


"I also prefer to have the f/1.4 for portraits and beautiful bokeh. The depth of field is an issue sometimes, but not enough for me to close the aperture too much." –[Andrew Fisher](https://www.instagram.com/andrewfisher7/) ,[What’s In My Bag: A Photo Kit For Rodeos, Western Lifestyle & More](https://alphauniverse.com/stories/whats-in-my-bag-a-photo-kit-for-rodeos-western-lifestyle-and-more/)


Photo by Andrew Fisher. Alpha 7R IV. 85mm f/1.4 G Master II.


##### 7.[Sony 70-200mm f/2.8 G Master II](https://electronics.sony.com/imaging/lenses/all-e-mount/p/sel70200gm2?utm_source=AlphaUniverse&utm_medium=Web&utm_campaign=Article)


###### Why It’s Great For Concert Photography


The[70-200mm f/2.8 GM OSS II](https://electronics.sony.com/imaging/lenses/all-e-mount/p/sel70200gm2?utm_source=AlphaUniverse&utm_medium=Web&utm_campaign=Article) is the go-to telephoto zoom for concerts when you need to work from the soundboard, a balcony or the back of the venue. It delivers the reach needed for tight compositions and compelling stage details, while the constant f/2.8 aperture and built-in stabilization support sharp handheld shooting in low light. It also gives photographers the flexibility to reframe quickly as performers move across a large stage.


###### Standout Features


- 70-200mm range reaches artists from distant shooting positions
- Constant f/2.8 aperture helps maintain exposure and shallow depth of field
- Optical SteadyShot with three modes provides added support for handheld work
- Four XD linear motors provide autofocus up to four times faster than the original model
- Approximate 1,045g weight keeps it highly portable for a professional 70-200mm f/2.8 zoom
- Compatible with 1.4x and 2x teleconverters for additional reach when needed


###### Creator Reviews


"This is my favorite lens of all time. Version I was originally my favorite lens of all time, but this is just lighter which is a huge help for me because I do carry two lenses on my body at all times. during a lengthy festival or a two- or three-hour show. So having that weight cut down is excellent. And I just love that I’m able to get really cool, tight intimate moments of artists because that’s the number one thing I’m looking for when shooting performances. I need to get some kind of emotion. I feel like I didn’t succeed if I’m not having the viewer feel what the artist is trying to convey in that photograph, and this lens allows me to do that. Also, I have some gaff tape on here because a lot of people shoot Sony at festivals and I don’t want to get my gear mixed up. And also sometimes the artist will see these little highlighter tape pieces. So sometimes it’s helpful to get directly at the camera." –[Greg Noire](https://www.instagram.com/gregnoire/) ,[Go Inside Greg Noire’s Ultimate Concert Photography Kit](https://alphauniverse.com/stories/go-inside-greg-noires-ultimate-concert-photography-kit/)


Photo by Greg Noire. Alpha 1. 70-200mm f/2.8 G Master II. 1/800-sec., f/7.1, ISO 250


"I LOVE this lens. It is hands down my favorite for concerts, especially when shooting outside of the photo pit. I’ll often pair this lens with the APS-C crop mode on my camera to get a little extra reach. It offers great compression in a super lightweight form factor." –[Reginald Cunningham](https://www.instagram.com/kidnoble) ,[What’s In My Bag: The Perfect Photography Kit For Concerts & Events](https://alphauniverse.com/stories/whats-in-my-bag-the-perfect-photography-kit-for-concerts-and-events/)


Photo by Reginald Cunningham. Sony Alpha 7CR. Sony 70-200mm f/2.8 G Master II. 1/500-sec., f/2.8, ISO 1250


"In concert photography, flexibility is key because you never know where you’ll be shooting from. Sometimes, publicists won’t tell you this information until you actually pick up your credentials at the venue, so you have to be prepared for anything. I’ve photographed at MSG before and was positioned right up against the stage, but this time, when I arrived, I was told that Cyndi was only allowing photos from the soundboard – which is all the way in the back of the arena. Without the reach of the 70-200mm, there’s no way I would’ve been able to get this image. That lens saved me." –[Dimitry Mak](https://www.instagram.com/dimitrymakphoto/) ,[Behind The Shot: A G Master Hero Shot Of Cyndi Lauper At MSG](https://alphauniverse.com/stories/behind-the-shot-a-g-master-hero-shot-of-cyndi-lauper-at-msg/)


Cyndi Lauper at Madison Square Garden - photo by Dimitry Mak. Sony Alpha 7R IV. Sony 70-200mm f/2.8 G Master II. 1/350-sec., f/2.8, ISO 640


##### 8.[Sony 135mm f/1.8 G Master](https://electronics.sony.com/imaging/lenses/all-e-mount/p/sel135f18gm?utm_source=AlphaUniverse&utm_medium=Web&utm_campaign=Article)


###### Why It’s Great For Concert Photography


When you need to isolate a performer from a distance, the 135mm f/1.8 GM is a standout concert prime. Its reach is ideal for larger stages, restricted-access venues and positions at the soundboard, while the bright f/1.8 aperture gives photographers the light-gathering ability needed to keep shutter speeds up under difficult stage lighting. The longer focal length also creates beautiful compression, turning spotlights, LEDs and haze into a dramatic background around the artist.


###### Standout Features


- 135mm focal length brings performers closer from the barricade, soundboard or balcony
- Bright f/1.8 aperture supports faster shutter speeds and lower ISOs in low light
- XD Linear Motor delivers fast, precise and quiet autofocus for performers in motion
- Premium G Master optics provide exceptional sharpness, contrast and smooth background rendering
- 11-blade circular aperture creates soft, expressive bokeh from stage lighting
- Approximately 950g weight makes it practical for handheld shooting throughout a set


###### Creator Reviews


"The bokeh goddess. It creates the perfect depth of field with telephoto compression. I love the cinematic feel of the frame that it creates and its ability to render detail is astonishing." –[Mickey Pierre-Louis](https://alphauniverse.com/member/#/itchyeyephotos) ,[What’s In My Bag: The Ultimate Camera Kit For Music & Portrait Shoots](https://alphauniverse.com/stories/whats-in-my-bag-the-ultimate-camera-kit-for-music-and-portrait-shoots/)


Photo by Mickey Pierre-Louis. Sony Alpha 7R V. Sony 135mm f/1.8 G Master.


"This lens is beautiful. I typically use this when I feel like I got what I needed, and I need a little bit more. So if I have a checklist in my mind of things that I need, once all bases are covered I’ll whip something like this out and get some more dreamier portraits. Because this thing at f/1.8 creates some of the most beautiful types of images I’ve ever had the pleasure of capturing. So this is something that doesn’t ever leave my Pelican case." – –[Greg Noire](https://www.instagram.com/gregnoire/) ,[Go Inside Greg Noire’s Ultimate Concert Photography Kit](https://alphauniverse.com/stories/go-inside-greg-noires-ultimate-concert-photography-kit/)


Photo by Greg Noire. Alpha 1. 135mm f/1.8 G Master. 1/800-sec., f/1.8, ISO 3200


Sony’s lens lineup is strong and this list is by no means exhaustive. What is your favorite Sony lens for live-music photography? Share your images and thoughts on social media with #SonyAlpha, and explore more lenses at[alphauniverse.com/lenses](https://alphauniverse.com/lenses/) .
